concept_html:
Azure Container Apps runs a container image behind an HTTPS address and scales it for you. One Azure CLI command deploys from your lab folder (Microsoft Learn, November 2025):

az login
az extension add --name containerapp --upgrade
az containerapp up --name survey-topics --source . --ingress external --target-port 8000

With --source, up creates a resource group, a Container Apps environment with a Log Analytics workspace, and an Azure Container Registry. It builds the image from your Dockerfile, pushes it, deploys it and prints the app's URL. Redeploy with the same command plus --resource-group and --environment.

Secrets. Define them on the app with --secrets "api-key=<value>", or better as Key Vault references. Pass them to the container as environment variables with --env-vars "MAX_BATCH=50" "API_KEY=secretref:api-key". Changing a secret does not create a new revision: restart the revision or deploy a new one to pick it up.

Health probes. Container Apps has startup, liveness and readiness probes. An HTTP probe passes on a status from 200 to 399. With ingress on, the default probes are TCP checks on the target port, which pass as soon as uvicorn listens, before the model has loaded. Point an HTTP readiness probe at /health, which answers 503 until the model is ready.

Scaling. With no rule of your own, an app scales on HTTP traffic from 0 to 10 replicas, adding a replica per 10 concurrent requests: ceil(concurrent / 10). At zero replicas you pay no usage charges, but the next request waits for a container to start and load the model. Set --min-replicas 1 when that wait matters.

Revisions. A change to the container template, such as a new image or scale rule, creates a new, immutable revision. Lesson B27-L6 uses revisions to roll back.

Delete the resource group when you finish practising, or it keeps costing money.

Write `env_var_args(plain, secret_refs) -> list[str]`, the items for `--env-vars`.

- `plain` maps variable names to values: `"MAX_BATCH=50"`.

exercises.prompt_html:
Write env_var_args(plain, secret_refs) -> list[str], the items for --env-vars.

  • plain maps variable names to values: "MAX_BATCH=50".
  • secret_refs maps variable names to secret names: "API_KEY=secretref:api-key".
  • Return all items sorted by variable name.
  • Raise ValueError if a variable appears in both, or any variable name is empty.
exercises.solution:
def env_var_args(plain: dict[str, str], secret_refs: dict[str, str]) -> list[str]:
    """Items for az containerapp --env-vars, secrets as secretref: references.

    Args:
        plain: Variable name to value.
        secret_refs: Variable name to the app secret it reads.

    Returns:
        NAME=value and NAME=secretref:secret items, sorted by name.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If a name is empty or appears in both mappings.
    """
    clash = set(plain) & set(secret_refs)
    if clash:
        raise ValueError(f"both plain and secret: {sorted(clash)}")
    if "" in plain or "" in secret_refs:
        raise ValueError("variable names must not be empty")
    items = {name: f"{name}={value}" for name, value in plain.items()}
    items |= {name: f"{name}=secretref:{secret}" for name, secret in secret_refs.items()}
    return [items[name] for name in sorted(items)]

exercises.prompt_html:
Write revision_name(app, suffix) -> str, returning "<app>-<suffix>" after checking the suffix against the Container Apps rules.

  • Only lower-case letters, digits and dashes.
  • Starts with a letter and ends with a letter or digit.
  • No two dashes in a row, and at most 64 characters.
  • Raise ValueError naming the suffix if any rule fails.
exercises.solution:
def revision_name(app: str, suffix: str) -> str:
    """A revision name, after checking the suffix rules.

    Args:
        app: Container app name.
        suffix: Revision suffix.

    Returns:
        "<app>-<suffix>".

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the suffix breaks a naming rule.
    """
    allowed = all(ch == "-" or (ch.isalnum() and ch.isascii() and not ch.isupper()) for ch in suffix)
    if (
        not suffix
        or len(suffix) > 64
        or not allowed
        or not suffix[0].isalpha()
        or not suffix[-1].isalnum()
        or "--" in suffix
    ):
        raise ValueError(f"invalid revision suffix: {suffix!r}")
    return f"{app}-{suffix}"
solution_lines: def revision_name(app: str, suffix: str) -> str:
"""A revision name, after checking the suffix rules.
Args:
app: Container app name.
suffix: Revision suffix.
Returns:
"<app>-<suffix>".
Raises:
ValueError: If the suffix breaks a naming rule.
"""
allowed = all(ch == "-" or (ch.isalnum() and ch.isascii() and not ch.isupper()) for ch in suffix)
if (
not suffix
or len(suffix) > 64
or not allowed
or not suffix[0].isalpha()
or not suffix[-1].isalnum()
or "--" in suffix
):
raise ValueError(f"invalid revision suffix: {suffix!r}")
return f"{app}-{suffix}"

title: Deploying the container to Azure Container Apps
why_html: A team deployed a model service with the default settings and saw the first request each morning time out. The app had scaled to zero overnight, and the cold start, including a 40-second model load, outlasted the caller's timeout. Setting a minimum of one replica for working hours removed the timeouts, and an HTTP readiness probe on /health stopped traffic reaching replicas whose model was still loading.
